mainTopic: פסח שני and פסח brought in טומאה: which laws carry over, הלל, overriding טומאה, and who is liable for eating or entering
overview: This amud finishes the כלל ופרט reading of the פסוק about פסח שני. The ban on eating the קרבן raw (נא) applies to פסח שני, but the ban on slaughtering it while owning חמץ does not, because a law about the offering itself takes priority. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules on הלל: there is no הלל at the פסח שני meal because that night is not a יום טוב, but הלל is said while slaughtering both offerings. Next it shows that our משנה, which holds that פסח שני does not override טומאה, goes against רבי יהודה, and it explains the reasoning of each side. A ברייתא that equates the two offerings is assigned to רבי יהודה, and a contradiction about לינה is resolved by saying two תנאים reported his view differently. A new משנה teaches that זבין, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat a פסח brought in טומאה but are exempt from כרת, and רבי אליעזר exempts them even for entering the מקדש. The גמרא brings the פסוקים behind both rulings. רב יוסף then asks whether טמאי מתים may enter the היכל, and רבא answers in two opposite versions. Finally רב יוסף begins a question about טמאים eating the אימורים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the general phrase add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which extra law the כלל ('ככל חקת הפסח') brings in for פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it including?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still reading the פסוק about פסח שני as a כלל ופרט. It now asks which law the general phrase adds beyond the details the פסוק lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כלל ופרט וכלל, the general phrase includes laws that resemble the listed details. The גמרא wants to know which specific law that turns out to be.

keyTerms.meaning: includes, adds in
a general phrase in a פסוק
the make-up פסח offering a month later

phrases.english: What is it including?
phrases.notes: Refers to the כלל: 'ככל חקת הפסח'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the כלל ופרט discussion earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the כלל adds for פסח שני.

steps.title: It adds the ban on eating the offering raw
steps.stepSummary: The כלל includes the prohibition of eating the פסח נא (half-roasted).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not eat from it raw.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the general phrase includes the ban on eating the פסח raw. That ban therefore applies to פסח שני too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on נא is about how the meat itself is eaten. That makes it similar to the listed details, such as not breaking a bone and not leaving meat over, so it fits inside the כלל.

keyTerms.meaning: half-roasted, not fully cooked

phrases.english: 'Do not eat from it raw.'
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ט

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on eating the פסח raw applies on פסח שני.

steps.title: What do the specific details leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law the פרט (the listed details) excludes from פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through its details, what is it excluding?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the other side of the question. If the general phrase adds something, what do the specific details exclude?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרט narrows things down. Laws that are not like the listed details are left out, and the גמרא wants to identify one.

keyTerms.meaning: a specific detail in a פסוק
excludes, leaves out

phrases.english: Through its details, what are they excluding?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the פרט excludes from פסח שני.

steps.title: It leaves out the ban on slaughtering with חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The פרט excludes the prohibition of slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not slaughter the blood of My offering with חמץ.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban on slaughtering the פסח while owning חמץ does not apply on פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח שני a person may own חמץ, since he only needs to remove it from his house on the first פסח. So slaughtering with חמץ around is not forbidden on פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: leavened bread
do not slaughter the פסח while owning חמץ

phrases.english: 'You shall not slaughter the blood of My offering with leavened bread.'
phrases.notes: שמות לד:כה

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חמץ prohibition at slaughtering does not apply to פסח שני.

steps.title: Why not reverse them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assignment: maybe the חמץ law is included and the נא law is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we decided this way. Maybe it is the other way around, so the חמץ law is included and the raw-meat law is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself never says which law goes on which side. Without a reason for the choice, the assignment seems arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it

phrases.english: I can reverse it!

steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of נא as included and חמץ as excluded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the פסוק forces this choice, so the reverse assignment seems just as possible.

steps.title: A law about the offering itself takes priority
steps.stepSummary: A מצוה connected to the body of the קרבן itself is the better one to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה about its own body is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the raw-meat law is about the meat of the פסח itself. That makes it the better choice to include, while the חמץ law is about something outside the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating raw concerns the קרבן's own meat. Owning חמץ concerns the owner's house, not the offering. When we must choose what the כלל brings in, the law that is closer to the offering wins.

keyTerms.meaning: a מצוה about the thing itself
is preferable, takes priority

steps.whatToRemember: For פסח שני, eating the meat raw is forbidden, but slaughtering while owning חמץ is allowed. The reason is that a law about the קרבן itself is preferred.

phrases.english: A מצוה of its own body is preferable.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two laws seem equal, so either one could be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: A law about the קרבן's own body is preferred for inclusion.

steps.title: Source for saying הלל while eating the first פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the first פסח needs הלל while it is eaten, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The first one requires הלל while it is eaten, etc.' From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks where we learn that הלל is said at the first פסח meal but not at the פסח שני meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. The גמרא wants a פסוק that explains why the two meals are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלל praise (תהלים 113 to 118)
from where are these things derived?

phrases.english: The first requires hallel when it is eaten, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the first פסח needs הלל while it is eaten and the second does not.

steps.title: Song on a night sanctified as a festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, derives from ישעיה that הלל is said only on a night that is a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: The פסוק says, 'The song will be yours as on the night a festival is sanctified.' A night sanctified as a festival requires הלל. A night not sanctified as a festival does not require הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ישעיה that links singing to a holy festival night. The first פסח night is יום טוב, so it gets הלל. The פסח שני night is not, so it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is whether that night is a יום טוב, not the קרבן itself. That explains why the same kind of meal gets הלל on one night and not on the other.

keyTerms.meaning: the song
a festival is sanctified
a night that is sanctified as a festival

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for saying הלל at the סדר on the night of פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
The verse says: 'The song shall be yours'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ל:כט

phrases.english: 'as on the night a festival is sanctified.'
A night sanctified for a festival requires hallel;

phrases.aramaic: לַיְלָה שֶׁאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג — אֵין טָעוּן הַלֵּל.
phrases.english: a night not sanctified for a festival does not require hallel.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישעיה ל:כט ties song (הלל) to a night that is sanctified as a festival.

steps.title: Why is הלל said while slaughtering both offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that both offerings need הלל while being prepared, and asks why this includes פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Both require הלל while they are being done, etc.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which says both the first פסח and פסח שני need הלל while they are slaughtered. It asks why פסח שני is included here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step taught that פסח שני is not a holy festival. So it seems surprising that it should get הלל at all.

keyTerms.meaning: while they are being done (slaughtered)
what is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה טְעוּנִין הַלֵּל בַּעֲשִׂיָּיתָן כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Both this and that require hallel when they are prepared, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why פסח שני needs הלל during its slaughter when it is not a festival.

steps.title: The פסוק only excludes the night
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the ישעיה פסוק excludes only nighttime הלל, not daytime הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it excludes the night, but it does not exclude the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The פסוק only speaks about the night, so it only removes הלל from the פסח שני meal. The daytime slaughter keeps its הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כליל' (as on the night) limit the exclusion to nighttime. Slaughtering happens in the afternoon, so the פסוק says nothing against הלל at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
night
day

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it excludes night,
it does not exclude day.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exclusion from the פסוק applies only to the night, so daytime slaughter still needs הלל.

steps.title: It is unthinkable to skip הלל
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: it makes no sense that כלל ישראל would bring their פסח or take their לולב without saying הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: Is it possible that ישראל slaughter their פסח offerings and take their לולבים, and do not say הלל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer based on plain logic. Such a great communal מצוה naturally calls for הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not rely on the wording of the פסוק at all. It argues that the moment itself demands praise, just like taking the לולב on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: is it possible?! (rhetorical)
palm branch taken on סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: There is no הלל at the פסח שני meal because that night is not a יום טוב. But there is הלל while slaughtering both offerings.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Is it possible that Israel slaughters their Paschal lambs
and takes their lulavim,
and they do not say hallel?!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is obvious from logic that such a communal מצוה is accompanied by הלל.

steps.title: Inference: שבת is overridden but טומאה is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about פסח שני overriding שבת and infers that it does not override טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they are eaten roasted, etc.' שבת, yes. טומאה, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה saying that both offerings override שבת. From the fact that only שבת is mentioned, it infers that פסח שני does not override טומאה. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists overriding שבת but says nothing about טומאה. That silence suggests that פסח שני cannot be brought while the people are טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: roasted
for שבת, yes
ritual impurity

phrases.english: And they are eaten roasted, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which goes on to say they override שבת.

phrases.english: Shabbat, yes; ritual impurity, no.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the wording of the משנה, פסח שני overrides שבת but not טומאה.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the משנה as going against the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states who the משנה does not agree with. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה holds that טומאה is not overridden, it cannot match a תנא who holds that פסח שני does override טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
not in accordance with

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה goes against רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבי יהודה says טומאה is overridden too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the תנא קמא says פסח שני overrides שבת but not טומאה, while רבי יהודה says it overrides טומאה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: It overrides שבת but does not override טומאה. רבי יהודה says: it even overrides טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous claim with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה holds פסח שני is brought even in טומאה, unlike our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה matches the first opinion in the ברייתא, the תנא קמא. רבי יהודה treats פסח שני like the first פסח, which can be brought in טומאה when most of the people are טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
overrides
even, also

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה holds that פסח שני overrides שבת but not טומאה. רבי יהודה holds that it overrides טומאה as well.

phrases.english: As it was taught: It overrides Shabbat,
and does not override ritual impurity.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It overrides even ritual impurity.

steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The reasoning of the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא holds that פסח שני does not override טומאה. It answers: a person who was pushed off because of טומאה should not turn around and bring the offering in טומאה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא? Because of טומאה I pushed him off, so should he now come back and bring it in טומאה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the logic of the תנא קמא from the ברייתא in step 14. That opinion is that פסח שני does not override טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of פסח שני is to help someone who was טמא on פסח ראשון. If we let him bring פסח שני while still טמא, the reason for pushing him off a month would make no sense. So for the תנא קמא, פסח שני must be brought in טהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The first (unnamed) opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
I pushed him off / deferred him
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?
Because of impurity I deferred him
phrases.notes: He was pushed off from פסח ראשון to פסח שני.

phrases.english: Shall he return and have it done in impurity?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: that would make no sense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the first side of the מחלוקת quoted in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Someone deferred because of טומאה should not end up bringing it in טומאה. So פסח שני does not override טומאה.

steps.title: The reasoning of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reasons that the Torah gave the person a second chance to bring the offering in טהרה. If he did not merit that, he brings it in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה: The Torah came back to him to let him do it in טהרה. If he did not merit it, let it be done in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the other side, the reasoning of רבי יהודה. He holds that פסח שני does override טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, פסח שני is an extra chance to bring the offering in טהרה. It is not a strict requirement of טהרה. If the second chance also fails, he should not lose the מצוה completely, so he brings it in טומאה, just like a community would on פסח ראשון.

keyTerms.meaning: Came back to him / sought him out again
Ritual purity
He did not merit it

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: פסח שני exists only for טהרה, so it does not override טומאה. רבי יהודה: פסח שני is a second chance at טהרה, and if that fails it is still brought, even in טומאה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda: the Torah came back to him
to let him do it in purity
if he did not merit it, let it be done in impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the second side of the מחלוקת, paired with step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah gave him a chance at טהרה. If he did not merit it, he still brings the offering in טומאה.

steps.title: A ברייתא equating the first and second פסח in three rules
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that פסח ראשון and פסח שני are the same in three ways: both override שבת, both override טומאה, and both require לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: פסח ראשון overrides שבת, and פסח שני overrides שבת. פסח ראשון overrides טומאה, and פסח שני overrides טומאה. פסח ראשון requires לינה, and פסח שני requires לינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that treats פסח שני exactly like פסח ראשון in three rules. This sets up the next two steps, which ask whose opinion this ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לינה means the person must stay in ירושלים overnight after eating the קרבן פסח and not go home until morning. The ברייתא says פסח שני needs this too. The key detail is that it says פסח שני overrides טומאה, which matches רבי יהודה from step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Overrides / pushes aside
Requires staying overnight in ירושלים
The regular קרבן פסח on 14 ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: Here לינה does not mean leaving meat overnight. It means the person himself must stay in ירושלים that night.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פֶּסַח רִאשׁוֹן דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: the first Pesach overrides Shabbat,
the second Pesach overrides Shabbat.
The first Pesach overrides impurity,
the second Pesach overrides impurity.
The first Pesach requires remaining overnight,
phrases.notes: Staying in ירושלים until morning.

phrases.english: the second Pesach requires remaining overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פֶּסַח רִאשׁוֹן דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא, related to the topic of steps 12-16 (פסח שני and טומאה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסח שני is like פסח ראשון in overriding שבת, overriding טומאה, and requiring לינה.

steps.title: This ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view holds that פסח שני overrides טומאה, and answers: רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says פסח שני overrides טומאה. Whose view is that? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the author of the ברייתא. Since it says פסח שני overrides טומאה, it must follow רבי יהודה. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From step 14 we know only רבי יהודה says פסח שני overrides טומאה. The תנא קמא disagrees. So this ברייתא must follow רבי יהודה, which means everything else in it, including לינה, should also be his view.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?

phrases.english: "Overrides impurity": in accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא in step 17, based on the מחלוקת in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, since only he holds that פסח שני overrides טומאה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה elsewhere says פסח שני needs no overnight stay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: another ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying פסח שני does NOT require לינה. He learns this from the פסוקים, because only the פסח followed by six days of מצה requires לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יהודה hold it requires לינה? Was it not taught: רבי יהודה says, from where do we know that פסח שני does not require לינה? It says, "And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents," and it is written, "Six days you shall eat מצות." The one that is followed by six days of eating requires לינה. The one that is not followed by six days of eating does not require לינה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. If the ברייתא is רבי יהודה's, it should not say פסח שני requires לינה, because רבי יהודה explicitly says it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the two פסוקים side by side. Going home in the morning is linked to the six days of מצה, which only exist after פסח ראשון. So only פסח ראשון requires לינה, and פסח שני, which has no seven-day holiday after it, does not. This clashes with the ברייתא in step 17, which we just assigned to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (in a ברייתא)? Introduces a contradiction
From where do we know?
And you shall turn in the morning (go home)
For six (days of eating מצה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real contradiction in רבי יהודה's view. The גמרא will now have to resolve it, either by changing who authored the ברייתא or by explaining how the two sources fit together.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, does it require remaining overnight?
But was it not taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין לְפֶסַח שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין טָעוּן לִינָה,
phrases.english: From where do we know that the second Pesach does not require remaining overnight?
As it is said: "And you shall turn in the morning
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ז

phrases.english: and go to your tents,"
and it is written: "Six days you shall eat matzot."
phrases.notes: דברים טז:ח, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: The one followed by eating for six days requires remaining overnight,
phrases.notes: That is פסח ראשון.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין נֶאֱכָל לְשִׁשָּׁה — אֵין טָעוּן לִינָה!
phrases.english: the one not followed by eating for six days does not require remaining overnight!
phrases.notes: That is פסח שני.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה טָעוּן לִינָה? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification in step 18 by pointing to a contradicting statement of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא in step 17, which says פסח שני requires לינה, follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה explicitly derives from the פסוקים that פסח שני does not require לינה. So a ברייתא saying it does require לינה cannot be his.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction between the two ברייתות is resolved: two different תנאים reported רבי יהודה's view differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19. It says the two ברייתות reflect two תנאים who report רבי יהודה's opinion differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says that in רבי יהודה's view פסח שני overrides טומאה and requires לינה. The other quotes רבי יהודה saying פסח שני does not require לינה. Instead of forcing them to agree, the גמרא says the תנאים simply disagree about what רבי יהודה held regarding לינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים. Two different teachers of the Mishnaic era.
According to the view of. Used when people argue about what a certain Sage held.
Staying overnight in ירושלים after bringing the קרבן.

steps.whatToRemember: When two ברייתות quote the same Sage in conflicting ways, the גמרא can answer 'תרי תנאי ואליבא ד־': each ברייתא follows a different report of that Sage's view.
steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים are not arguing about their own opinions. They are arguing about what רבי יהודה's opinion was.

phrases.english: There are two tannaim
and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: The dispute is specifically whether רבי יהודה required לינה on פסח שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the attribution: two תנאים transmit different versions of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to quote one consistent רבי יהודה, so they looked contradictory about לינה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא's report of רבי יהודה. The contradiction disappears.

steps.title: משנה: זבין and similar may not eat a פסח brought in טומאה, but have no כרת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that זבין, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat a פסח brought in טומאה, but if they ate it they are exempt from כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the קרבן פסח is brought in טומאה, זבין, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat from it. If they did eat, they are exempt from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It addresses a פסח brought while most people are טמא, and who may and may not eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the people are טמא מת, the פסח is brought anyway, and the טמאי מת may eat it. Other kinds of טומאה, such as זב, נדה and יולדת, are not permitted, so these people still may not eat. However, eating קדשים in טומאה normally carries כרת, and here they are exempt from כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן פסח offered in טומאה, because most of the nation is טמא מת.
Men and women who are טמא because of an unusual bodily discharge.
Women who are טמא from menstruation or from childbirth.
Spiritual 'cutting off.' The usual punishment for eating קדשים while טמא.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that once the פסח is brought in טומאה, every טמא person may eat it. Only the טומאת מת is permitted. זבין and similar are still forbidden. The only difference is that they do not get כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two things that usually go together: 'forbidden to eat' and 'punished with כרת.' Here the eating is still forbidden, but the כרת does not apply.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The Paschal lamb that comes in impurity,
phrases.notes: Because most of the people are טמא מת.

phrases.english: may not be eaten from by
zavim, zavot, menstruating women, and women after childbirth.
But if they ate —
they are exempt from karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a פסח brought in טומאה, זבין, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat it, but if they do, they are exempt from כרת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר exempts them even for entering the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds these טמאים are also exempt from כרת for entering the מקדש in this situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר exempts them from כרת even for entering the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: Still in the משנה, רבי אליעזר adds a further exemption. He says these people are exempt from כרת even if they enter the מקדש while טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a טמא person who enters the מקדש gets כרת. Because the טמאי מת are allowed in on this day, רבי אליעזר extends the exemption to זבין and similar people who enter. They are still not supposed to enter, but they would not get כרת for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש. When done in טומאה, this normally carries כרת.
Exempts from punishment.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer exempts them
even for entering the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹטֵר אַף עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a broader opinion to the exemption in the first part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: in a פסח brought in טומאה, these טמאים are also exempt from כרת for entering the מקדש.

steps.title: ברייתא: Might they be liable for כרת?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא raises the possibility that זבין and similar who ate a פסח brought in טומאה would be liable for כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if זבין, זבות, נדות or יולדות ate from a פסח brought in טומאה, one might think they are liable for כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that is the source for the משנה's exemption. This line sets up the question, and the next line gives the answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starting assumption is reasonable. These people are not allowed to eat this פסח, and a טמא person eating קדשים normally gets כרת, so we would expect כרת here too. The ברייתא raises this so it can show from the פסוק why כרת does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This introduces a ברייתא.
One might have thought. This introduces an initial assumption that will be rejected.
Liable to punishment.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
Zavim, zavot, menstruating women, and women after childbirth
who ate from a Paschal lamb that came in impurity,
one might think they would be liable to karet —

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן זָבִין וְזָבוֹת נִדּוֹת וְיוֹלְדוֹת שֶׁאָכְלוּ בְּפֶסַח שֶׁבָּא בְּטוּמְאָה יָכוֹל יְהוּ חַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's search for the source of the משנה's exemption from כרת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are זבין and similar who ate a פסח brought in טומאה liable for כרת?

steps.title: The verse links כרת to meat that pure people eat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cites ויקרא ז:יט-כ, where the כרת for eating in טומאה follows right after 'every טהור may eat the meat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Every טהור person may eat the meat. And the soul that eats meat from the שלמים offering that belongs to ה', with his טומאה upon him, will be cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק. The full explanation of how the פסוק proves the exemption is spelled out in the text that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת for eating in טומאה appears right after 'כל טהור יאכל בשר.' This suggests the כרת applies only to meat that is normally eaten by טהורים. A פסח brought in טומאה is eaten by טמאים, so eating it in טומאה does not bring כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches. This introduces the verse that settles the question.
Every pure person may eat the meat (ויקרא ז:יט).
With his טומאה upon him. The condition for כרת.
And it will be cut off. The source of the כרת punishment.

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption from כרת comes from the order of the פסוקים: the כרת for eating in טומאה is tied to meat that טהורים eat.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
"Every pure person may eat the meat.
But the soul that eats meat
from the peace-offering that belongs to the Lord,
with his impurity upon him, shall be cut off."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר כׇּל טָהוֹר יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'יכול' question from step 23 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק places the כרת for eating in טומאה right after 'כל טהור יאכל בשר.' This implies כרת applies only to meat that טהורים eat, and that excludes a פסח brought in טומאה.

steps.title: The verses' order shows when eating in impurity brings כרת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes its reading of the verses: כרת for eating in טומאה applies only to a קרבן that is normally eaten by טהורים, not to a פסח brought in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the offering is eaten only by pure people, impure people are liable for eating it because of their impurity. But if it is not eaten only by pure people, impure people are not liable for eating it because of their impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out what it learns from the verse quoted in step 24. The זבין, זבות, נדות and יולדות who ate a פסח brought in טומאה are not liable for כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת for eating in טומאה comes right after 'every טהור may eat the meat,' so the two are linked. כרת applies only when the meat is limited to טהורים. A פסח brought in טומאה is open to טמאים, so the כרת does not apply there, even to people with other kinds of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: eaten only by pure people (the normal case)
liable (for כרת) for eating while impure
spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating קדשים while impure

steps.whatToRemember: The כרת for eating קדשים in טומאה applies only when the קרבן is limited to טהורים. A פסח brought in טומאה is not limited that way, so זבין and the others who eat it are exempt from כרת, though they still may not eat it from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: Being exempt from כרת does not mean they may eat it. The משנה (step 21) said these טמאים may not eat it in the first place. The ברייתא only removes the punishment.

phrases.english: If it is eaten by the pure,
phrases.notes: A normal קרבן, which only טהורים may eat.

phrases.english: they are liable for it because of impurity;
but that which is not eaten only by the pure,
phrases.notes: A פסח brought in טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין טְמֵאִין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם טָמֵא.
phrases.english: impure people are not liable for it because of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱכַל לִטְהוֹרִים — חַיָּיבִים עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal conclusion from the verse cited in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: זבין and the others who eat a פסח brought in טומאה are exempt from כרת, because כרת applies only to food limited to טהורים.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר considers liability for זבין who push into the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר raises the possibility that זבין who forced their way into the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה would be liable for כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One might think that if זבין pushed their way in and entered the courtyard during a פסח brought in impurity, they would be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the source for רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה (step 22). It starts with an assumption, 'יכול,' that the Torah will soon reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only טמאי מתים were allowed to enter during a פסח brought in טומאה. זבין have a more severe טומאה and were not part of that permission. So we might think they are still liable for כרת for entering the מקדש while impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'one might think', which introduces an assumption that will be rejected
they pushed or forced their way in
men with a זיבה discharge, a severe form of impurity
the Temple courtyard where the קרבנות are offered

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One might think, if zavim pushed
and entered the courtyard
during a Pesach brought in impurity,
one might think they would be liable;

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל דָּחֲקוּ זָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from liability for eating to liability for entering the מקדש. This is the source for רבי אליעזר's view from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are זבין who force their way into the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה liable for כרת?

steps.title: The verse links זבין and מצורעים to טמאי מתים
steps.stepSummary: From במדבר ה:ב, which lists צרוע, זב and טמא לנפש together, רבי אליעזר learns that when טמאי מתים are not sent out, זבין and מצורעים are not sent out either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'That they send out from the camp every צרוע, every זב, and everyone impure from the dead.' When those impure from the dead are sent out, זבין and מצורעים are sent out. When those impure from the dead are not sent out, זבין and מצורעים are not sent out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own assumption with a verse. The three types of טמאים are listed together, so the rule for sending them out is shared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the verse groups all three together, their exclusion from the מקדש goes together. During a פסח brought in טומאה, טמאי מתים are not sent out. So זבין and מצורעים who push in are also exempt from כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the verse teaches', which introduces the source that rejects the assumption
'and they shall send out from the camp' (במדבר ה:ב)
a person with צרעת (a leper)
a person impure from contact with a dead body
are sent out

steps.whyThisMatters: According to רבי אליעזר, the permission of טומאה for the פסח also removes the punishment from more severe טמאים who force their way in, even though they were never allowed in to begin with. The תנא קמא of the משנה does not give this exemption for entering.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"That they send out from the camp
every leper and every zav
and everyone impure by the dead";
at a time when those impure from the dead are sent out,
zavim and lepers are sent out;
when those impure from the dead are not sent out,
zavim and lepers are not sent out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וִישַׁלְּחוּ מִן הַמַּחֲנֶה כׇּל צָרוּעַ וְכׇל זָב וְכֹל טָמֵא לָנָפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption from step 26 with a verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Because the verse groups the three types of טמאים together, זבין and מצורעים are not sent out when טמאי מתים are not, so they are exempt from כרת.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks about טמאי מתים entering the היכל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether the permission for טמאי מתים to enter the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה also covers the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: If people impure from the dead pushed in and entered the Sanctuary during a Pesach brought in impurity, what is the law? Since impurity in the courtyard was permitted, was impurity in the Sanctuary also permitted? Or perhaps only what was permitted is permitted, and what was not permitted stays forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a new question with two possible sides. The question is how far the permission of טומאה reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עזרה had to be opened to טמאים because that is where the פסח is offered. The היכל plays no role in the פסח. One side says the permission covers the whole מקדש. The other side says the permission is only as wide as the need, so the היכל stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (a real question of uncertainty)
the Sanctuary building, holier than the courtyard
was permitted
or perhaps (introduces the second side)
what is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
If those impure from the dead pushed
and entered the Sanctuary
during a Pesach brought in impurity, what is the law?
Since impurity in the courtyard was permitted,
impurity in the Sanctuary was also permitted?
Or perhaps what was permitted is permitted,
and what was not permitted is not permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: דָּחֲקוּ טְמֵאֵי מֵתִים וְנִכְנְסוּ לַהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea of permitted entry from step 27 and asks whether it reaches beyond the עזרה into the היכל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the permission of טומאה in the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה also cover the היכל, or only the area that was actually needed?

steps.title: רבא: 'from the camp' means even from part of the camp
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the verse that the obligation to send out טמאים applies even to part of the מחנה, so the היכל stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says 'They shall send out from the camp,' which means even from part of the camp.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles רב יוסף's question with a reading of the verse. The answer is that only what was permitted is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מן' ('from') shows that sending out can apply to a portion of the מחנה. So even when טמאים are allowed into the עזרה, they must still stay out of the היכל, and one who enters it is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse says
part of the camp
camp (here, areas of the מקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: During a פסח brought in טומאה, טמאי מתים may enter the עזרה. According to רבי אליעזר, זבין and מצורעים who push in are also not liable. In this first version of רבא's answer, the היכל stays forbidden, because 'מן המחנה' teaches that the sending out applies even to part of the מחנה. The next step brings a second version that disagrees.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'even part of the camp' as a stricter rule for the עזרה. It means the permission is partial: the עזרה is opened, while the rest (the היכל) stays closed.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"They shall send out from the camp",
even from part of the camp.
phrases.notes: The word 'from' implies a portion of the camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: וִישַׁלְּחוּ מִן הַמַּחֲנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question from step 28, choosing the second side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permission is only partial. Even when טמאים may enter the עזרה, they are still sent out of the היכל, so טמאי מתים who enter it are liable.

steps.title: A second version of רבא's answer: the היכל is not forbidden either
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, רבא reads the verse differently. The partial sending-out (from the היכל) applies only where the full sending-out (from the whole camp) applies. Since טמאי מתים are not sent out of the camp during a פסח brought in טומאה, they are not barred from the היכל either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רבא said, the verse says 'That they send out from the camp … outside the camp you shall send them.' Anywhere we apply 'outside the camp you shall send them,' we also apply 'they shall send out from the camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's answer to רב יוסף's question about the היכל. This version reaches the opposite result from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 29, רבא used the phrase 'send out from the camp' to show that טמאים must be kept out even of part of the camp, so the היכל stays forbidden. In this version, the two phrases are tied together. The partial removal ('from the camp') applies only when the full removal ('outside the camp') also applies. During a פסח brought in טומאה, טמאי מתים are not sent out at all, so they are also not barred from the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say', which introduces a second version of a statement
'We read it about this case', meaning the verse applies here
'That they send out from the camp', which can mean removal even from part of the camp
'Outside the camp you shall send them', which means full removal from the whole camp

steps.confusionAlert: Step 29 and step 30 are two versions of the same answer by רבא, and they reach opposite results. In step 29 the היכל stays forbidden. In this version the היכל is not forbidden either. Do not try to combine them into one view.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions disagree about how far the permission of טומאה goes when most of the people are טמא. The question is whether the permission covers only the עזרה, or the היכל too.

phrases.english: Some say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second version of the answer in step 29, and it reaches the opposite result.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the permission for טמאי מתים to enter the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה also cover the היכל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The partial removal applies only where the full removal applies, so when טמאים are not sent out of the camp, the היכל is not forbidden either.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks about impure people eating the altar portions
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks a new question. If טמאי מתים pushed their way in and ate the אימורים of a פסח brought in טומאה, what is the law? The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: if people made impure by a dead body pushed their way in and ate the altar portions of a פסח brought in טומאה…
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins a new question about טמאי מתים who ate the אימורים of a פסח brought in טומאה. This step only sets up the case. The actual question is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about entering places: the עזרה and the היכל. Now the topic moves to eating. The אימורים are meant to be burned on the מזבח, not eaten, and eating them can carry a penalty. רב יוסף wants to know whether the permission of טומאה changes anything when טמאים eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He asked', which introduces a real question
'They pushed', meaning they forced their way in
The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח, such as the fats and kidneys
People made impure by contact with a dead body
